newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee says Q2 weak at all 3 units.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee says Q2 weak at all 3 units.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp said Thursday that lower second-quarter earnings reflected weaker operating income in all three of its business units -- exploration and production, chemicals and coal.
The company reported operating earnings today of $0.66 per share, versus $0.91 share in the year-earlier period.

In a statement accompanying the earnings report, chief executive Luke Corbett said, "The largest decline was in coal, where operating profit was down $13 million due to a production halt in one of the Galatia Mine's two longwall systems because of an underground ignition. The mine safely resumed full production in mid-July."

Lower oil production and natural gas sales volumes and lower oil price realization contributed to a $4 million decline in exploration and production operating profit for the second quarter, said the company.

It also noted that operating profit from chemicals declined $4 million from the prior-year quarter due to lower prices for titanium dioxide pigment and higher operating expenses. While previously announced price increases for pigment took effect in the second quarter, Kerr-McGee said they have not yet rebounded to second-quarter 1996 levels.
